name: PNUTS
aliases: Platform for Nimble Universal Table Storage
tagline: Yahoo's geo-replicated record store (2008) that introduced per-record timeline consistency.
description: PNUTS was Yahoo's massively parallel, geographically distributed data-serving platform for web applications, described in a VLDB 2008 paper and run internally under the name Sherpa. It offered a simplified relational model of tables of flexible-schema records, stored in hash or ordered tables partitioned into tablets across storage units, with data replicated asynchronously between regions over Yahoo's own message broker. Its signature idea was per-record timeline consistency: each record has a master region that serializes its updates, and applications choose per call between read-any, read-critical, read-latest and test-and-set writes to trade latency against freshness. It was never released outside Yahoo, but its per-call menu of consistency levels became a recurring theme in later NoSQL and geo-replicated systems.
statusNote: Yahoo-internal system (2008 onward, also called Sherpa); never released publicly and its current internal status is unknown.

scale.notes: Tablets spread across storage units in multiple data centers; each record is mastered in one region.

strengths: Per-record timeline consistency: a practical middle ground between strong and eventual
Per-call choice of read freshness versus latency
Designed from the start for multi-datacenter replication
weaknesses: Writes to a record must route to its master region, adding cross-region latency
useCases: Background reading for designing geo-replicated stores
notIdealFor: Any deployment: there is no public implementation
